title: Masoor Dal (Madhur Jaffrey)
summary: A simple, fragrant red-lentil dal finished with a tarka of cumin seeds, dried chillies and asafoetida. Adapted from Madhur Jaffrey via The Happy Foodie.
instructions: Pick over the lentils for grit, then wash in several changes of water and drain.
Place the lentils in a heavy-based pan with 1.2 litres of water and the turmeric. Stir and bring to a simmer. Cover with the lid slightly ajar.
Cook over low heat for 35–40 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally.
Add the salt, mix, and leave covered over very low heat.
Heat the ghee or oil in a small frying pan over fairly high heat. Add the asafoetida and then the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add the chillies and cook until they turn dark red — just a few seconds. Pour the contents of the pan over the lentils and stir.

title: Creamy Chicken Korma with Almonds (Madhur Jaffrey)
summary: A mildly spiced korma with a blended almond-and-ginger paste, finished with single cream and garam masala. Adapted from Madhur Jaffrey's Simple Indian Cookery via The Happy Foodie.
instructions: Skin the chicken pieces and cut into serving portions; set aside.
Blend the garlic, ginger, almonds and 6 tablespoons of water into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the bay leaves, cardamom pods, cloves and cinnamon stick and stir for 10 seconds.
Add the onion and cook, stirring, until browned.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the almond paste with the cumin, coriander and cayenne. Stir for 3–4 minutes, then add the tomato purée and stir for a minute longer.
Add the chicken, salt, cream, garam masala and 150 ml of water. Bring to a simmer, cover, reduce the heat to low and simmer gently for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the cinnamon stick and bay leaves before serving.

title: Aloo Gobi (Madhur Jaffrey)
summary: Punjabi-style cauliflower and potatoes with garlic, ginger, fenugreek and green chillies. The cauliflower and potatoes are deep-fried first for a deeper flavour. Adapted from Madhur Jaffrey via The Happy Foodie.
instructions: Heat the sunflower oil in a karhai or wok over medium-high heat until very hot. Fry the cauliflower florets in two batches for about 2 minutes each until light brown. Drain on kitchen paper, allowing the oil to reheat between batches.
Carefully add the potato to the hot oil and fry for 5–6 minutes until golden. Drain on kitchen paper. Strain and reserve the oil.

In a clean karhai or heavy-based pan over medium heat, pour in 2 tablespoons of the oil. Add the onion and sauté for 2 minutes. Add the cumin seeds and stir for 3–5 minutes until the onion is light brown.
Add the garlic and ginger, stirring for 2 minutes (add a splash of water if needed to prevent sticking).
Add the tomato and cook for 5 minutes until fully integrated.
Sprinkle in the chillies and salt and stir for 1 minute. Crumble in the fenugreek leaves and stir for another minute. Add the turmeric and mix well.
Add the cauliflower stalks and leaves and cook, stirring, for 6 minutes until soft (add water if the pan dries out).
Add the deep-fried cauliflower florets, potato and coriander. Mix gently and cook for a final 2 minutes before serving.

title: Saag Paneer (Madhur Jaffrey)
summary: Spinach cooked gently with a ginger-garlic-chilli paste, finished with golden-fried paneer cubes and a touch of cream. Adapted from Madhur Jaffrey via The Happy Foodie.
instructions: Blend the ginger, garlic and green chilli with 50 ml of water until smooth using a blender or food processor.

Heat the oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Fry the paneer pieces until golden brown on all sides, turning gently. Remove with a slotted spoon and sprinkle with one-eighth of a teaspoon of salt, the garam masala and the cayenne pepper.
Add the blended paste to the hot oil, stirring constantly for 30 seconds. Add the spinach and half a teaspoon of salt. Stir for 1 minute.
Cover the pan, lower the heat and cook the spinach gently for 15 minutes. Add a splash of water if the pan dries out.
Add the paneer and cream, stir gently and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
